section: India - soil types, characteristics and distribution; soil erosion and conservation
subsections: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes sheet erosion?
o: Subsurface removal of soil resulting in sinkholes
Formation of deep trenches by concentrated surface flow
Downslope movement of soil under gravity
Removal of a thin, uniform layer of topsoil by overland flow
accepted.x: Sheet erosion removes a thin top layer uniformly through overland flow. It is widespread and generally the least noticeable form of erosion.
accepted.tq: Use the process-based definition to distinguish closely related erosion types.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding erosion types:
1. Rill erosion produces small channels cut by running water.
2. Wind erosion involves deflation, saltation and surface creep.
3. Tunnel erosion is caused by subsurface removal and may create sinkholes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Rills are small water-cut channels, wind erosion involves the three stated movements, and tunnel erosion removes soil below the surface and can form sinkholes.
accepted.tq: Test several process definitions together and select the inclusive code only after checking each statement.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of water erosion in the correct sequence:
A. Gully erosion
B. Splash erosion
C. Rill erosion
D. Sheet erosion
o: B, D, C, A
D, B, C, A
B, C, D, A
D, C, B, A
accepted.x: Water erosion generally progresses from splash to sheet, then rill and finally gully erosion.
accepted.tq: Use the progression from dispersed impact to increasingly concentrated flow.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chambal — gully erosion
Thar Desert — wind erosion
Himalayan monsoon slopes — mass erosion
Parts of Australia and Africa — sheet erosion
accepted.x: Parts of Australia and Africa are associated with tunnel erosion, in which subsurface removal may create sinkholes, not sheet erosion.
accepted.tq: Find the regional example that does not correspond to the stated erosion process.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s: Which of the following represents the correct order of increasing soil loss generally associated with the main forms of water erosion?
o: Rill, splash, sheet, gully
Splash, sheet, rill, gully
Gully, rill, sheet, splash
Sheet, splash, gully, rill
accepted.x: The usual progression of increasing soil loss is splash, sheet, rill and gully erosion. Water is described as the most powerful erosion agent in this context.
accepted.tq: Arrange processes by increasing intensity and concentration rather than by their visual size.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s: Wind erosion is generally most severe under which combination of conditions?
o: Mulched soil, low wind speed and frequent light rain
Waterlogged soil, gentle winds and heavy forest cover
Bare, dry, fine-textured soil with strong and frequent winds
Dense vegetation, moist clayey soil and weak winds
accepted.x: Wind erosion is worst where soil is bare, dry and fine-textured and winds are strong and frequent.
accepted.tq: Combine the environmental conditions instead of identifying a single isolated factor.
accepted.sec: Soil erosion types (sheet, rill, gully, wind) - regions → erosion type, order of soil loss

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Conservation method)
 a. Contour ploughing
 b. Terracing
 c. Check dams
 d. Shelter belts

List-II (Function)
 i. Trap sediment and check gully growth
 ii. Tree rows that reduce wind speed
 iii. Ploughing along contour lines to slow runoff
 iv. Steps cut on steep slopes

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–iii, b–iv, c–i, d–ii
a–iv, b–iii, c–ii, d–i
a–iii, b–i, c–iv, d–ii
a–ii, b–iv, c–i, d–iii
accepted.x: Contour ploughing slows runoff along contour lines; terracing creates steps; check dams trap sediment and limit gully growth; shelter belts reduce wind speed.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure process-function pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatch.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s: Strip cropping primarily involves:
o: Planting only trees in long strips across a watershed
Constructing permanent dams across every field channel
Removing crop residues before ploughing
Alternating erosion-resistant crop strips, such as grass, with row-crop strips
accepted.x: Strip cropping alternates strips of erosion-resistant crops, such as grass, with row crops to reduce wind- and water-induced erosion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a field-layout method from structural and tree-based conservation measures.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about conservation agriculture:
1. It may involve minimum or zero tillage.
2. Crop residue is retained as soil cover.
3. Mulch helps stabilise the soil.
4. It necessarily requires complete removal of crop residues.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Conservation agriculture uses minimum or zero tillage, retains crop residues and uses mulch for soil stability. Complete removal of residues is contrary to the practice.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the central principle of the conservation method.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with a national soil and watershed-related programme or initiative?
o: Soil Health Card — construction of coastal shelter belts only
IWMP — watershed development approach
Desert Development Programme — replacement of all agricultural land by forests
RKVY — classification of Himalayan landslides only
accepted.x: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme is associated with the watershed development approach. The other descriptions do not represent the stated programmes or initiative.
accepted.tq: Identify the genuine programme-function relationship and reject exaggerated or exclusive descriptions.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s: The Watershed Development Component of PMKSY was formed by merging IWMP during:
accepted.x: IWMP began in 2009–10 and was merged in 2015–16 into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY.
accepted.tq: Separate the programme’s starting year from the year of institutional merger.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s:
Which of the following are included in the watershed approach associated with the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY?
1. Ridge-area treatment
2. Drainage-line treatment
3. Soil and moisture conservation
4. Linking all perennial rivers of the country
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
accepted.x: The approach includes ridge-area treatment, drainage-line treatment, and soil and moisture conservation. Linking all perennial rivers is not one of the listed components.
accepted.tq: Separate actual watershed-treatment components from an unrelated large-scale water-transfer claim.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s: Biochar used in soil conservation is associated with which of the following effects?
o: Increased wind speed at the soil surface
Complete elimination of soil erosion without vegetation
Lower water-holding capacity and higher soil nitrous oxide emissions
Higher water-holding capacity and an approximately 30–50% reduction in soil N2O emissions
accepted.x: Biochar raises the soil’s water-holding capacity and is associated with a reduction of soil N2O emissions of about 30–50%.
accepted.tq: Use the paired positive effects and numerical range to identify the precise option.
accepted.sec: Soil conservation methods

accepted.s: Mining-led deforestation is particularly associated with land degradation in which group of States?
o: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
accepted.x: Mining-led deforestation is associated with Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. The other groups represent different or unsupported patterns.
accepted.tq: Match the specific land-degradation cause with its regional concentration.
accepted.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mining-led deforestation — Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha
Overgrazing — Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
Over-irrigation — Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
Climate change — only Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Climate change is a general additional driver of land degradation and is not confined only to Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. The other pairs correctly reflect the stated associations.
accepted.tq: Watch for the restrictive word “only” when testing a broad causal factor.
accepted.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

accepted.s: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India is produced by which organisation?
o: Forest Survey of India
National Disaster Management Authority
Space Applications Centre of ISRO
Indian Council of Agricultural Research
accepted.x: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas is produced by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who produces this report or atlas?’ identification method.
accepted.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the finding on sustainable soil-management practices in the FAO 2026 assessment?
o: They were equally worsening and improving in 75 countries.
They were worsening in about 10% of assessments and improving in 58%.
They were worsening in 58% of assessments and improving in only about 10%.
They were improving in all assessments.
accepted.x: The assessment reported worsening sustainable practices in 58% of assessments and improvement in only about 10%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the larger deterioration percentage from the much smaller improvement percentage.
accepted.sec: Land degradation causes → state and Desertification Atlas

accepted.s: Which factor generally has a greater influence on soil erosion than the total annual amount of rainfall?
o: Atmospheric pressure alone
Annual mean temperature alone
Rainfall intensity
Length of the frost season alone
accepted.x: Rainfall intensity matters more than total annual rainfall because intense bursts can exceed the soil’s infiltration capacity and generate runoff.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between rainfall intensity and total rainfall, the key conceptual pair.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about factors controlling erosion:
1. Slope gradient influences the rate of soil erosion.
2. Vegetation cover and land use influence erosion.
3. Soil type and texture influence erosion.
4. Total annual rainfall is always more important than rainfall intensity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Slope, vegetation and land use, and soil type and texture are important factors. Statement 4 is false because rainfall intensity generally matters more than total annual rainfall.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed comparison in the final statement after checking the valid controlling factors.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

accepted.s: Very intense bursts of rainfall can make soil drier because they:
o: Always infiltrate completely and recharge the soil
Exceed infiltration capacity, causing runoff or evaporation instead of recharge
Convert all soil organic carbon directly into clay
Prevent surface water from moving downslope
accepted.x: When rainfall intensity exceeds infiltration capacity, water runs off or evaporates rather than recharging the soil. This drying effect can offset the benefit of greater annual rainfall.
accepted.tq: Apply the infiltration-excess mechanism to an observed rainfall scenario.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about erosion estimation is correct?
o: RUSLE is used exclusively for earthquake prediction, and ICAR has prepared mineral maps.
RUSLE predicts long-term water erosion on slopes, and ICAR has prepared national cover-management and slope-factor maps.
RUSLE predicts only wind erosion in deserts, and ICAR has prepared only rainfall maps.
RUSLE measures only annual temperature, and ICAR has prepared only forest-fire maps.
accepted.x: RUSLE is used to predict long-term water erosion on slopes. ICAR has prepared national cover-management (C) and slope (P-factor) maps for erosion estimation.
accepted.tq: Match the model and institutional mapping work with their precise purposes.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

accepted.s: A 2026 study applied RUSLE together with GIS to study erosion in the hills of:
o: The Thar Desert only
North-East India
The Lakshadweep Islands
The Malwa Plateau only
accepted.x: A 2026 study paired RUSLE with GIS for studying erosion in the hills of North-East India.
accepted.tq: Use the geographic application area to distinguish the study from unrelated physiographic regions.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between soil properties, slope and carbon?
o: Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, while steep slopes can lose carbon-rich topsoil.
Sandy soils always hold more soil organic carbon than clay soils, and steep slopes conserve topsoil.
Clay soils cannot retain soil organic carbon.
Slope has no relation to the loss of carbon-rich topsoil.
accepted.x: Clay soils hold more soil organic carbon, whereas steep slopes are more prone to losing carbon-rich topsoil.
accepted.tq: Test the paired comparison between soil texture and slope-related carbon loss.
accepted.sec: Factors controlling erosion rate - rainfall intensity vs total, slope, vegetation cover
